input.overview: The original 1975 El Dorado is a moving-light drop-target game. A lit drop scores 5,000 instead of 500, and the spot moves as switches score. Completing the required bank or banks scores 5,000, resets the targets, and lights Special; the required completion differs between three- and five-ball play. Soft-plunge the lit upper-right 5,000 lane, then keep choosing the currently lit target over unlit progress.
input.simpleOverview: In the original 1975 El Dorado, soft-plunge the lit upper-right lane for 5,000. Then shoot whichever drop target is lit: it scores 5,000 instead of 500. Completing the required top bank or both banks scores 5,000, resets the targets, and lights Special. Three- and five-ball settings change the completion requirement, so check the card first.
input.summary: Track the moving 5,000 light and shoot the lit target from the safer flipper. Use a flying backhand only when a right-bank feed will not trap. Finish the qualifying bank once only a few targets remain, then resume lit-target scoring after the reset.

quickInfo.name: Three-ball completion
quickInfo.summary: The top bank can qualify the reset and Special, depending on the installed card.

quickInfo.name: Five-ball completion
quickInfo.summary: Complete both target banks for 5,000, reset, and Special.

quickInfo.name: Moving spot
quickInfo.summary: Switch scoring advances which target or lane is lit.

steps.text: Soft-plunge the lit upper-right lane for 5,000.
Locate the moving 5,000 light and shoot that drop from the flipper with the cleanest angle.
Read each side feed before flipping; nudge slow right-side returns away from the inlane-outlane divider.
When only a few required drops remain, finish the qualifying bank or banks for 5,000 and a reset.
After the reset lights Special, favor fresh lit drops unless the award shot is already safely lined up.

buildsToward.title: Repeatable lit-target scoring and a reset bank

steps.text: Collect 5,000 lit drops while reducing the required bank.
Complete the top bank in the applicable three-ball setup or both banks in five-ball play.
Use the reset targets for another sequence of lit 5,000 shots.

machineSetup: Identify the original 1975 El Dorado rule set before using this route; Target Alpha, Solar City, Canada Dry, Gold Strike, Lucky Strike, and the later solid-state remake share geometry but change scoring or awards.

Confirm three- or five-ball play and whether card B-16143 or B-16144 is installed, then test both drop banks, moving spot, lit values, completion reset, Special lamps, pop-bumper values, upper-right skill lane, and all three side feeds.

quickInfo.name: Three-ball completion
quickInfo.summary: The top bank can qualify the reset and Special, depending on the installed card.

steps.text: Knock down drop targets for 300 points each and 1,000 bonus per target. Target lights mark drops already knocked down; they do not increase target value.
End-of-ball bonus doubles on the last ball. Completing the drops does not raise them again during that ball.
With the drops down, the top lane remains worth 5,000 points; bumpers score 100.

checkBeforePlay: Confirm the game is Solar City; shared-layout Target Alpha and El Dorado have different scoring.

steps.text: Knock down the upper targets for 2,000 each and the side targets for 500 each. Each drop adds 1,000 bonus, doubled on the last ball. Target lamps mark drops already made; they do not increase target value.
Completed targets stay down for the rest of the ball. Bonus is counted and the targets reset between balls. The upper lane scores 5,000.

On the three-ball extra-ball card, clearing the upper bank lights the right Extra Ball rollover and Special rollover. Clearing the side bank lights the left Extra Ball rollover. Roll through a lit award rollover to collect; this setup allows one extra ball per ball in play.

checkBeforePlay: Check the installed card and extra-ball settings; the documented B-17245-1 setup awards an extra ball for Special.
